items.title: 52060_Eddie Barefield oral history interview
items.q: So when I went to Milwaukee I came in contact with this fellow, Earl Keith

ctx.x: Were metal clarinets more common those days?

Well, it was something more durable, you know. But I played it in the upper register and then I played in the low register but I didn't know anything about the bridge, you know. So when I went to Milwaukee I came in contact with this fellow, Earl Keith, who I said was a marvelous clarinet and saxophone player. And so I met Eddie Inge and he was a marvelous clarinet player and he gave me my first lesson on a clarinet. Then when I took Eddie Inge's place with Bernie Young's orchestra and went to Chicago and we were…
So now back to where we were --
